details.label: Summary
details.text: Isolated damaging wind gusts are possible into the evening. The severe wind threat is expected to remain too isolated for watch issuance

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Numerous thunderstorms have developed along a surface boundary across the region with over 3000 J/kg of MLCAPE (per RAP-based mesoanalysis). Although these storms are developing in a weak-shear environment, the thermodynamic environment supports a threat of wet microbursts. As these storms pulse up and subsequently collapse, damaging wind gusts will be possible over the next couple of hours. Cold-pool clustering, as storms push to the southeast, may enhance the damaging wind threat. Given the isolated spatiotemporal severe-weather threat (ending shortly after dark), a severe-thunderstorm watch is unlikely

details.label: Most probable threats
details.text: MOST PROBABLE PEAK WIND GUST...UP TO 60 MPH

details.label: Summary
details.text: The risk for severe wind and hail will continue across western and central SD over the next several hours. An instance of 2+ inch diameter hail or a 75+ mph gust is possible

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Multicells and supercells continue to progress across western and central SD. Several severe gusts have been reported, with MRMS MESH data suggesting hail over 1.5 inches diameter has fallen from some of the stronger storms. A buoyant and sheared airmass precedes the ongoing storms, with 1500+ J/kg MLCAPE coinciding with 45-60 kts of effective bulk shear over much of central SD. The current thinking is that supercell structures will be maintained for at least a few more hours, accompanied by a severe wind/hail threat. The best chance for severe, including significant severe wind/hail, will be with the more sustained, mature supercells currently over central and northwestern SD

details.label: Most probable threats

details.label: Summary
details.text: The threat for damaging winds will continue over the next few hours as storms cluster across the area

details.label: Discussion
details.text: The development of numerous storms in a moist, unstable environment in the lee of the Appalachians have slowly clustered and grown upscale this afternoon. Within a modestly favorable low-level westerly shear environment (i.e., 0-3 km shear around 20-25 knots per mesoanalysis and local VWPs), continued upscale growth and organization is likely over the next few hours. As such, the threat for damaging winds will persist as multiple clusters progress eastward toward the higher terrain

details.label: Most probable threats
details.text: MOST PROBABLE PEAK WIND GUST...55-70 MPH
